title: 100 prisoners. 100 boxes.
blocks: A hundred prisoners, a hundred boxes. Each box hides a random prisoner's number. Each prisoner may open fifty boxes. If everyone finds his own number, all go free. If one fails, all are lost.
Opening boxes at random, each prisoner succeeds half the time. All hundred succeeding is one in two to the power of a hundred. Essentially zero.
But there is a plan. Each prisoner opens the box with his own number first. Inside is another number. He opens that box next, and so on, following the chain, up to fifty boxes.
Every box points to another one, so the numbers form loops. A prisoner finds his number if his loop has fifty boxes or fewer.
So everyone survives exactly when no loop is longer than fifty. For a random arrangement of a hundred, that happens about thirty-one percent of the time.
From odds of basically zero to nearly one in three, just by using the numbers inside the boxes as directions. Structure beats luck.
